summary: Embedding ingest window rotation causing intermittent rerank candidate suppression and p99 tail latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent empty or highly truncated rerank responses (missing candidates + severe p99 latency spikes) for a subset of queries sent to the reranking endpoint. Problem started ~2026-03-09 23:00 UTC and has recurred several times since under peak load.

Impact:
- DocuAnswers (dedicated customer) experiences ~0.8% of user queries returning 0-2 candidates instead of expected top-10, plus p99 latency > 12s for rerank calls.
- Downstream UX shows missing results and retries, increasing user-visible errors.
- No billing anomalies reported but operational availability degraded for some requests.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) in us-west-2 on dedicated fleet.
- Ingest path: docu-embed-producer -> grpc-ingest-proxy -> embedding-ingest-service -> embedding-store -> reranker.
- Reranker configured to merge external metadata by candidate ID.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1. Send batched ingestion of long articles split into 20+ chunks (chunk size ~512 tokens) using the customer SDK with chunk-windowing enabled.
2. Immediately call /rerank with the new embedding namespace and same candidate IDs.
3. Intermittent runs return fewer candidates or empty top-k and show 5xx/timeouts in the rerank pipeline.

Observed behaviour:
- Reranker logs show candidate ID lookup misses for many IDs that were just ingested.
- Embedding-store returns hits for the same IDs if queried directly within a short window, but query ordering differs from the reranker merge step.
- p99 latency for rerank escalates when ingest concurrency > 50 and batch-chunk-count > 16.
- Correlated spikes in grpc-ingest-proxy CPU and occasional header rewrite logs.

Expected behaviour:
- Newly-ingested embeddings should be discoverable and included in rerank responses consistently within configured consistency window.

Relevant logs/metrics/links:
- Customer provided example request IDs: req-7f3a2c, req-7f3a5b, req-7f3a8d (attached to ticket).
- Grafana dashboards: /d/redwood/embeddings?var-customer=DocuAnswers (p99 and miss-rate panels).
- Slack thread: #support (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0123456).

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Reduce ingest chunk-windowing to <= 12 chunks per batch and backoff concurrent ingest writers.
- Retry rerank calls after 2s when results are empty.

Notes on urgency:
- Customer is on Dedicated with an SLA; impact is material to production UX. Engineering and SRE already looped in for immediate triage.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Ingested ticket from DocuAnswers. Customer provided three failing request IDs and a short trace. They say it started after a SDK update last week but still reproducible intermittently under load.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Marco Velez (SRE, assignee): Acknowledged. Kicking off probe: will reproduce in staging with same ingest pattern and high concurrency. Assigned to investigate grpc-ingest-proxy and embedding-store consistency windows.

2026-03-10 13:42 - Eng (ingest-proxy team): Initial findings: under high concurrency the proxy rotates internal ingestion window offsets to balance chunk routing. There's a legacy header (X-Embed-Window) rewrite that can happen when chunk_count > 16. Hypothesis: header rewrite causes mismatch between candidate IDs in metadata vs stored embedding keys, leading to soft misses in merge step.

2026-03-10 14:30 - SRE (Marco): Reproduced in staging using DocuAnswers workload. Observed ID remapping in proxy when chunk_count = 20 and concurrent writers >= 60. Repro rate ~30% in stress test. Added logging patch locally to trace header values across proxy and ingest-service boundary.
2026-03-11 08:11 - Customer (DocuAnswers): Confirmed that reducing concurrent writers significantly reduced frequency. They requested timeline for a permanent fix and asked about any data loss risk.

2026-03-11 12:22 - Eng (ingest-proxy team): Root cause narrow: a recent micro-optimization introduced an in-place buffer rotate that reused the X-Embed-Window header slot; under race the header could be updated after ID hash computation but before store write, causing mismatched keys. No evidence of durable data loss; embeddings are stored but metadata mapping can point to the wrong embedding shard until a natural TTL/refresh or retry.

2026-03-11 15:50 - Marco Velez (SRE): Created hotfix branch to make header updates copy-on-write and added an invariant check asserting header immutability for multi-chunk ingests. Hotfix PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/6789. Planning rolling restart for proxy fleet in the affected private deployment window 2026-03-12 03:00-03:30 UTC.

2026-03-12 02:15 - Operations: Rolling restart executed in us-west-2 private nodes. Post-deploy synthetic tests show no reproduction at previous load levels. Customer notified of planned verification window.

2026-03-12 09:00 - DocuAnswers: After the restart and recommended SDK backoff, they report no further empty-rerank incidents in the 24h verification window. Requesting closure when monitoring is stable for additional 48h.

2026-03-12 11:05 - Marco Velez (SRE): Leaving ticket in In Progress until long-tail verification completes. Follow-up tasks created for postmortem and adding e2e ingest->rerank test coverage for chunk_count permutations.
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced in staging with scripted generator using same chunking parameters.
- Key observation: when chunk_count > 16 and concurrency high, X-Embed-Window header mutated in-place inside grpc-ingest-proxy.
- Reranker merge relies on stable candidate ID hash and metadata mapping; header mutation changed routing/shard computation in-flight.
- No persistent loss: embeddings were written but metadata lookup used stale/incorrect key for a short interval.
- Mitigation validated: make header update copy-on-write, assert immutability, add additional logging around candidate-id -> shard mapping.
- Tests to add: e2e tests for chunk_count values [8,12,16,20,32] under concurrency 10..200 and unit test for header immutability.
resolution: Hotfix applied to grpc-ingest-proxy to prevent in-place header mutation (PR #6789). Rolling restart performed for affected private nodes in us-west-2. Post-deploy synthetic load tests show reproduction rate dropped to 0/1000 runs with previous failure pattern. Recommended follow-ups: add e2e tests (assigned INT-430), instrument long-tail monitoring for 7 days, and document chunking limits in the SDK release notes. Customer asked for 48h additional monitoring window; will move to Resolved after verification. No data loss found; issue classified as bug in ingest-proxy micro-optimization.
